meta.question: Class imbalance & drift — how extreme and how stable is the fraud rate across time and splits?
Amount structure — do fraud and non-fraud amount distributions differ, and by how much?
Temporal concentration — when (hour / weekday / month / era) does fraud concentrate?
Geography — is risk spatially structured (state, city, ZIP3, card→merchant distance)?
Cardholder behavior — do velocity / history signatures separate fraud from genuine activity?
Categorical risk structure — which categories, states, jobs and merchants carry elevated risk?
Unsupervised separability — do embeddings, clusters and anomaly scores isolate fraud without labels?
Causal predictive ceiling — what leak-free performance is achievable and which feature families drive it?

meta.title: Data contracts evaluated with actual min/max printed (FIX #5)
Schema audited; identifiers (cc_num/zip/trans_num) excluded from numeric analyses
Class imbalance: train 7506/1296675 = 0.5789%, test 2145/555719 = 0.3860% — extreme imbalance, drift between splits detected
Temporal split: train ends 2020-06-21 12:13:37, test starts 2020-06-21 12:14:25 — time-series CV is REQUIRED for any modeling (walk-forward implemented in §08)
999 cards × ~1,471 median txns — repeated-measures structure ⇒ card-clustered inference (§06) is mandatory
merchant → category is deterministic (collinearity): merchant-level effects are category-level effects + noise from finite counts

Merchant coordinates are per-transaction jitter (no fixed store locations): any card→merchant distance signal is a property of the noise model, not geography — reported honestly wherever dist_km is used (see §07)
Fraud amounts are strongly shifted right vs non-fraud (see §06 effect sizes: Cliff's delta with bootstrap CI)
COVID window (Mar–Jun 2020) fraud-rate shift quantified vs adjacent windows
Night hours (00–06) show markedly elevated fraud rate vs volume share (see phase1_hour figure + §06 forest plot with CIs)
State-level fraud-rate gradient exists but small-n states shrink toward baseline under EB — geographic claims restricted to well-populated states
Age gradient in fraud rate quantified by bin (see figure + §06 MW test with effect size for age)
Category × hour interaction: online-shopping-type categories concentrate fraud in the 22:00–06:00 window (see heatmap)
dist_km separates classes (KS D=0.007) BUT is generator noise per §01 forensics — discriminative signal is an artifact of the simulator's fraud coordinate sampling, not physical travel
zip3 regional structure: 1 states max per zip3 (purity=100.0%); zip3 EB rates add granularity beyond state for high-volume prefixes
Per-card fraud rate is bimodal: 2.3% of cards never defrauded, 97.7% defrauded at least once — fraud is card-clustered, not exchangeable across transactions

GENERATOR ARTIFACT (do NOT transfer as a prior): 97.7% of cards have ≥1 fraud event on this dataset — Sparkov gives fraud to nearly every card, which is the OPPOSITE of production card data where most cards never see fraud. Card-level fraud rates here are a property of the simulator's per-card fraud-minting process, not of real cards
Money lens: total fraud exposure $5,121,414; Gini=0.418; top-1% fraud txns = 2.3% of $ loss
Fraud-dollar ranking by category (not just count) — review-budget tables in §08 use $ capture, not only recall
MI ranking: behavioral/velocity features rank alongside amount — motivates the ablation experiment in §08
Cramér's V: category vs target strongest categorical association; merchant↔category V≈1.0 (deterministic, §01) — drop one in modeling
STL: weekly seasonality strength = 0.21 in daily fraud rate (trend + seasonality + residual plotted separately)
Autocorrelation: daily volume lag-7 = 0.87 (weekly periodicity); fraud-rate lag-1 = 0.50 — evidence of temporal clustering of fraud
Structural breaks in daily fraud-rate stable across PELT penalties (2 consensus breaks); holiday proximity: 0 coincidences — breaks are generator-campaign driven, not calendar-driven

Fraud is LESS likely than genuine txns to follow >72h card silence (0.2% vs 0.6%; ratio 0.32) — among fraud txns that have a prior txn on the same card, 90.7% follow another FRAUD txn — the mechanism is rapid clustering, not dormancy: it is genuine spending that resumes after dormancy. The visual 'bursts after dormancy' impression from card timelines is quantitatively wrong (direction auto-graded from the data)
Embedding separability: best = PCA(2) (logistic AUC 0.816); embeddings show partial fraud structure but no clean separation — consistent with noisy-overlap fraud signatures
K-Means (k=3): densest cluster reaches 1.9× baseline fraud rate — clusters capture some risk structure but no pure-fraud cluster
Clustering stability: hierarchical vs K-Means ARI = 0.74; DBSCAN finds 1 clusters + 4% noise — structure is dominated by volume, not by fraud
Unsupervised anomaly detection isolates fraud only weakly (AUCs 0.731–0.881): fraud is contextual relative to card history, not pointwise-outlying — motivates per-card features (§07)
Amount shift quantified: Cliff's delta = 0.669 [bootstrap CI 0.656, 0.680], KS D = 0.724 [0.715, 0.732], BH-q = 0
Categorical associations with target: category V=0.067 > state > gender — effect sizes (not just p) reported per plan §7.2
Hour forest: night hours carry statistically robust rate elevations (Wilson CIs exclude baseline after BH correction)
Category forest identifies the high-risk merchant categories with CIs — the forest plot is the primary evidence table for categorical risk
Cluster-robust logit (cards as clusters, n_cards=961): 5 of 8 effects survive card-clustered SEs — per-transaction effects are smaller than naive SEs suggest (repeated-measures structure matters)
Velocity features are the strongest behavioral signals: fraud rate rises monotonically with implied speed and with trailing-window counts (see next figure)

Interpretation boundary: dist_km carries signal only because the generator jitters merchant coordinates per transaction and samples the jitter differently for fraud events — a property of the simulator, NOT of real-world geography. Distance features must be re-validated on real data.
Hour-encoding comparison (ADDED): raw vs sin/cos vs one-hot PR-AUC 0.859 / 0.859 / 0.847 — cyclical is compact; one-hot marginally better if the hourly profile is non-smooth
Leakage demo: naive group-mean TE correlates with the test target at ρ=0.048 vs causal ρ=0.048 — every published pipeline using full-data target encodings on this dataset overstates its signal
Interaction check: night + risky categories + amt≥500 multiplies risk 42× vs baseline — interactions materially beat main effects (SHAP interactions in §08 for the model view)
Cohort analysis: fraud risk varies by card age (early-card months differ from mature months) — see cohort heatmap; campaign-like arrival quantified next via survival analysis

Time-to-first-fraud: hazard peaks at month 23 (48.889% vs flat 8.721%) — compared AGAINST the flat baseline hazard (FIX #8), so the 'fraud arrives early after card entry' claim is now supported rather than asserted; note this remains consistent with both campaign timing and generator card-aging, not proof of the former
Customer lifetime: median 556 transactions before the first fraud; 9.3% of defrauded cards are hit on their very first transaction
Repeated-fraud: 0.0% of affected cards experience ≥2 distinct fraud events; event-size distribution shows bursty multi-txn compromises rather than persistent re-fraud
Merchant hierarchical EB (merchant∈category): shrinking toward the category EB prior prevents small-n merchants from dominating risk rankings — top merchants are consistently risky, not lucky
Zip3→state hierarchy verified (100% single-state zip3s): zip3 rates are a consistent refinement of state rates for downstream encoding

Adversarial validation achieves held-out AUC = 1.000 (FIX #3) — train and test are (near-)perfectly separable by cumulative-history features (top: te_category, te_state, n_prior). Every train→test metric in this notebook (final PR-AUC, ablation delta, learning curve) measures out-of-distribution transfer under temporal drift, NOT typical generalization; walk-forward CV within the train period is the honest generalization estimate, and the ablation / learning-curve deltas must be read through this OOD lens

PSI per feature confirms which features drive the AUC=1.000 adversarial split: 7 of 27 features are SEVERE (PSI≥0.25) — top: month_sin=6.51, n_prior=5.10, month_cos=1.45. This corroborates the ablation: expanding target encodings and cumulative-history counts carry the train/test drift, so their within-model weight is a drift signal rather than a fraud signal
Walk-forward CV (time-ordered, 4 folds): PR-AUC 0.9510 ± 0.0152 — single-carve-out estimates would understate variance (review rigor item)

OOD transfer quantified (FIX #10): the SAME fold models score PR-AUC 0.951±0.015 in-domain but 0.473±0.076 on the held-out test split — mean OOD gap = +0.478 per fold. This is the cleanest single number for 'within-train generalisation minus cross-boundary transfer' and should be cited whenever anyone quotes a single train→test metric on this dataset

Leak-free causal model — test PR-AUC = 0.5575, ROC-AUC = 0.9677 (expanding TE + velocity features, train-only prior; all published numbers on this dataset that use full-data encodings are not comparable)
Time-decay weighting (half-life 180d): PR-AUC 0.5408 vs unweighted 0.5575 — recency weighting hurts on OOD test

Monotonic constraints (4 constraints on fraud-directional features: log_amt, is_night, cnt_24h, card_prior_fraud): PR-AUC 0.5922 vs unconstrained 0.5575 — helps accuracy while making the model audit-compliant
Fold-ensemble vs single final model: PR-AUC 0.5128 vs 0.5575 — single wins under OOD transfer
Calibration: Brier = 0.00241, ECE = 0.0019 — probabilities are reasonably trustworthy (review rigor item)
Temperature scaling (T=1.418) improves ECE from 0.0002 to 0.0001 on the early-stopping split — calibration is materially improved post-hoc
Bootstrap 95% CI on test PR-AUC: [0.5365, 0.5784] around 0.5575 (n_boot=200) — the point estimate is a specific sample, not a generalisation claim (FIX #13)

Leave-card-out CV (FIX #14): PR-AUC drops from 0.9948 on seen cards to 0.9639 on held-out cards (Δ = 0.0308) — the model uses per-card history that doesn't fully transfer to genuinely new customers; test rows of held-out cards score 0.5541. ((a) is partially in-sample, so the seen-vs-held gap is an upper bound on the new-customer penalty)
Cost-sensitive operating point: threshold 0.0000 minimizes expected loss (FP $5 friction vs full fraud amount) — recall 0.842 with $92,044 missed

Cost sensitivity (FIX #12): the cost-min threshold is fragile under FP-cost assumptions from $1 to $50 (threshold ratio 443.6×, optimal thresholds 0.0000–0.0004) — 70.2%–91.6% recall range across the sweep
Review budget: flagging top 1% of test by score captures 65.5% of fraud events and 68.7% of fraud dollars

Learning curve is NON-MONOTONIC: test PR-AUC peaks at frac=0.25 (n=324,168, PR-AUC=0.627) then falls to 0.525 on the full train set (drop 0.101) — more train-period data does NOT help, because train→test is a distribution shift (see the adversarial-validation finding: near-perfect split separability). All train→test metrics here measure OOD transfer; the walk-forward CV numbers are the honest generalization estimate

Decomposed ablation (FIX #11): the biggest single contributor to the OOD failure is 'MINUS card_prior_fraud' — removing it recovers PR-AUC by +0.2740 (0.5575 → 0.8315). All-family deltas vs raw-only: FULL (all features)=-0.278; MINUS card_prior_fraud=-0.004; MINUS te_* (4 features)=-0.168; MINUS cnt_*/n_prior (3 features)=-0.270; MINUS velocity (4 features)=-0.150. This localises the drift mechanism: card_prior_fraud is what does not transfer across the split
SHAP: top drivers are the behavioral/TE block (te_category, card_prior_fraud, cnt_24h...) + amount — consistent with the ablation
Segment errors at the operating point: weakest recall in health_fitness, kids_pets, personal_care — where fraud is rare or amounts are small (see table for state/hour breakdowns)
The leakage-demo claim is not supported by its own numbers
